project.name: Flysos downloadable legal-document replacement, claim workflow, and priority update

currentChange.name: Required questionnaire answers, Goftino widget settings, claim deletion, downloadable legal-document replacement, claim priority, claim-registration connection repair, admin runtime module-graph repair, questionnaire submit cache correction, registration SMS template editing, ten-minute flight scheduler repair, admin flight-monitor latest-flight ordering, stage-four receipt CMS editing, and inline responsible-expert assignment
scope: Require every visible cancellation or delay questionnaire question to be answered before save and final submission.
Expose questionnaire section metadata in authenticated admin claim responses and views.
Expose, validate, and conditionally persist the Goftino widget identifier without a database migration.
Restore the existing admin claim-delete action with supervisor-only, transactional server behavior without deleting shared customer/history data.
Allow safe replacement of either downloadable legal document with transactional activation and post-commit physical-file cleanup without deleting database data.
Persist the admin claim summary handling priority through the existing authenticated claim-update transaction without changing database contents.
Replace the native missing-question browser alert with an inline accessible red validation message above the active questionnaire.
Harden MySQL pool/transaction lifecycle and return after file persistence while queueing OCR and registration notification work; no schema or data change.
Use one cache-key-stable shared React entry module for public and admin routes so the admin bundle cannot instantiate a second React runtime.

Expose the existing registration SMS template in General Settings, preserve the existing backend rendering/persistence contract, and deploy only the static asset update without changing database contents.
Run the flight-cache scheduler every ten minutes, expose its effective interval in protected diagnostics, and preserve the last valid stored snapshot during provider failures.
Deploy the scheduler configuration without database changes and identify the remaining provider-server reachability blocker from production logs.

Expose the supervisor-only team-performance report, load it when the Reports screen opens, include every claim-handling staff member shown in Expert Management, calculate assignment/closure/review-time metrics from current claims and status history, and keep satisfaction explicitly unregistered until survey data exists.
Order admin flight-monitor rows from the newest valid cache snapshot with the latest scheduled flight first while preserving the existing ten-minute provider GET scheduler and public flight contract.
Update the direct Multer dependency to 2.4.0 after validation identified a high-severity multipart advisory; preserve all upload contracts and lock the patched production version.
Make the mandatory stage-two ticket-upload error visible immediately below the stage heading and scroll it into view after a blocked continue action without changing stage-three behavior.
Expose the final stage-four receipt text through the editable track-success CMS block and apply published values only to the generated receipt canvas while preserving dynamic claim data.

Add a supervisor-visible responsible-expert selector to every claims-table row, load the existing expert list on the claims screen, persist changes through the existing authenticated claim-update endpoint, and preserve row navigation and non-supervisor read-only behavior.

claimRegistrationConnectionFollowUp.name: Claim registration database connection, timeout, and notification repair
scope: Prevent OCR and registration notification work from extending the core claim HTTP request.
Harden MySQL pool and transaction cleanup for stale or fatal connections without adding unsafe write retries.
Deploy the repair and verify health without submitting a real production claim.
rootCause: Ticket OCR ran synchronously in the multipart request and could exceed the cPanel/reverse-proxy timeout, surfacing as a generic Request failed response.
The submit path waited for post-commit SMS/template work and performed a second claim read, allowing provider or stale-connection delays to make a committed claim appear failed.
Transaction begin ran outside the cleanup guard and rollback failure could mask the original database error, leaking or reusing a broken pool connection.

architectureDecisions: Keep the existing prebuilt frontend asset pair and repair the backend contract rather than rebuilding unavailable frontend source.
Keep public and admin imports on one exact cache-key-stable React entry URL; query-string differences on the same physical bundle are treated as separate module instances.
Use passengerRightsUrl as the public/API name and rightsDocumentUrl as the canonical AppSetting storage column.
Store new CMS media under the CMS subdirectory and keep claim uploads outside public static serving.
Allow generic PDF MIME values only with a PDF extension and verify the uploaded PDF signature before persistence.
Reuse the existing HTTPS flight push architecture and MySQL flight-cache tables, with a shared advisory lock for pull and push synchronization.
Keep the larger request-body bound scoped to the flight import route and preserve the 1 MB limit for unrelated JSON APIs.
Enforce visible questionnaire completeness at both questionnaire save and final claim submission without changing the database schema.
Expose questionnaire section and localized section-label metadata in admin claim mappings while retaining existing answer fields.
Expose the Goftino widget identifier through the settings contract and use a read-only column check before persistence.
Validate and normalize SMS inputs, preserve SMS history, map provider failures, and keep SMS secrets server-side.
Deny direct public access to backend source/log files at the document-root layer while preserving /api routes.

Restrict claim deletion to supervisors, delete claim-owned rows transactionally, detach nullable cross-feature history, preserve shared customers, and remove uploaded files only after safe upload-root validation.

Resolve only the two downloadable legal-document slots, commit new CmsMedia plus the matching AppSetting URL together, and clean the previous unshared physical file only after commit without deleting metadata.
Reuse the existing Claim.priority column with closed-set validation and a parameterized transaction branch; no migration or data mutation is required.
Keep OCR and registration notification work outside the core claim request, return from committed state, and harden MySQL pool/transaction cleanup without blanket retries for non-idempotent writes.
Expose registration SMS editing through the existing protected settings contract and reuse AppSetting.smsTemplates without a schema or data migration.
Use one guarded in-process flight scheduler with a bounded ten-minute default, preserve the last valid cache on provider failure, and expose only interval/attempt metadata to admin diagnostics.
Prefer direct provider refresh when reachable; otherwise use the existing authenticated HTTPS import push path from the provider-accessible server.
Scope admin flight-monitor ordering to the cache-summary read path: newest fetch first, latest scheduled flight first, and no public API ordering change.
assumptions: The configured MySQL database is available to deployment and can run the idempotent legal-document migration.
Existing root-level CmsMedia filenames are generated server-side and can be safely resolved through the legacy allow-list route.
The active browser bundles in the repository are the deployed frontend assets.
risks: No MySQL server or production credentials are available for live migration/API verification in this workspace.
